item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: The Not So Well Known Megillah of Hanukkah - Megillat Antiochus
item.description:
Is there a scroll for Hanukkah? Megillat Antiochus, attributed by Rav Saadiah Gaon to the sons of Matityah and by the Baal Halachot Gedolot to the students of Hillel and Shammai, tells of Nicanor, Bagris, Yohanan and Matityah himself going to war. It is not in Tanakh or the Talmud, yet it was read publicly in Italy and by the Yemenites, and it is worth reading on Hanukkah.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 5: Daily Halacha: Is Matityahu Ashkenazi?
item.description:
Two differences in the text of Al HaNissim. Is it Matityah or Matityahu? The Terumat HaDeshen writes Matityahu, but the Beit Yoseph rules Matityah, as in Tanakh and the Sepharadi siddur, which is how a get is written for Sepharadim. Is Hashmonai a description of Yohanan or a second name? Ashkenazim, the Hida and the Ben Ish Hai read it as a description, while the old Spanish and Portuguese siddurim, followed by Hakham Ovadiah, take it as his second name.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 6: Daily Halacha: Writing a Get for Someone Named מתתיה and the Correct Pronunciation of חנוכה
item.description:
Was the hero of Hanukkah called Matityah or Matityahu? The question matters when writing a get, where names must be exact. The Terumat HaDeshen rules Matityahu, as people say it, while the Beit Yoseph writes Matityah, as in Tanakh and the Sepharadi Al HaNissim, so Sepharadim write one get with Matityah and Ashkenazim, in doubt, give two.

item.title: 7: Daily Halacha: The Battle of Beauty
item.description:
The Greeks and the Hasmoneans fought over beauty. Scripture admires beauty yet Mishlei calls charm false and beauty vain, and the Hida offers an interpretation of that verse. Hanukkah teaches beautifying misvot, the extra candle each night, so that outer beauty reflects something within.

item.title: 10: Daily Halacha: Lighting the Menorah Late at Night
item.description:
When should the Hanukkah menorah be lit, and what if one is late? The Shulhan Arukh's time is the end of sunset, just after half past four in London this year, ideally within about half an hour while people are still in the street. Since we now light mainly for the household, one may light with a berakhah all night until dawn; the Mishnah Berurah and the Ben Ish Hai want someone in the family awake, but Hakham Ovadiah allows lighting even alone.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 11: Daily Halacha: Lighting the Menorah from Right to Left or Left to Right
item.description:
In which direction should the Hanukkah lights be lit? Following the Gemara's principle, codified by the Rambam, of always turning to the right, the Shulhan Arukh has the new light of the night, on the left, lit first with the berakhah, moving from left to right; this is the universal Sepharadi practice, held by the Arizal too. The Vilna Gaon begins with the first, main light, nearest the doorway, and lights from right to left, so Ashkenazi practice varies.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 12: Daily Halacha: When Sepharadim Don't Follow Rambam & Why They Light One Menorah Per Family
item.description:
Why do Sepharadim light one menorah for the whole family? The Gemara sets three levels: one light per household each night, one per person, and the finest, adding a light each night. The Rambam combines the top two, so that each person adds a light, and the Rema follows him for Ashkenazim; unusually, the Shulhan Arukh follows Tosafot, so that the night can be recognised, and the head of a Sepharadi household lights for everyone.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 14: Daily Halacha: Children Away from Home: Can They Rely on Their Parents' Lighting?
item.description:
Does a Sepharadi child studying away need to light Hanukkah candles? If still financially dependent, he relies on his parents, even across time zones, and lights without a berakhah, intent not to rely does not help. If he is ahead in time he may light with a berakhah. Ashkenazim each light.

item.title: 15: Daily Halacha: Saying the Blessings of the Menorah on Just Seeing the Menorah
item.description:
Why is the menorah unique among the misvot? Someone who only sees Hanukkah lights burning says SheAsah Nissim, though he cannot say the berakhah on lighting. The Rambam applies this to anyone not lighting himself that night, but the Shulhan Arukh, because of doubt over berakhot, follows the Rashba: only when no one is lighting for him at home either, as for a traveller who sees menorahs in the street.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 21: Daily Halacha: Using Oil from Israel This Year for Lighting Menorah

item.title: 27: Daily Halacha: Praying for Rain Part 1: Why the Date Is Based on the Secular Calendar
item.description:
Why is the start of asking for rain outside Israel the one date in halacha fixed by the civil calendar? In Israel the request begins on 7 Heshvan, but outside Israel the Hakhamim set it sixty days after Tekufat Tishrei, the halachic autumn, which follows the solar year. By Shmuel's length of the year, the Beit Yosef, quoting Rabbi David Abudarham, gives 22 November, a date later shifted by the Gregorian reform, as the next class explains.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 29: Daily Halacha: Praying for Rain Part 3: The Southern Hemisphere
item.description:
How do communities in the southern hemisphere, where the seasons are reversed, pray for rain? Rav Yaakov Meir, the first Rishon LeSion of the British Mandate, simply reversed the northern practice, but this is not followed today. Most Sepharadim there, as Hakham Ovadiah favours, say Morid HaTal and Barekhenu all year and add the request for rain in Shema Kolenu in their winter, while Ashkenazim generally pray as in the north, for Kelal Yisrael as a whole.
Daily Halacha — Hanukkah Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Hanukkah series.

item.title: 32: Daily Halacha: Lighting the Menorah from Right to Left or Left to Right
item.description:
Do you light the Hanukkah menorah from left to right or right to left? The Shulhan Arukh says to begin with the new candle on the far left and turn rightward, following the Talmudic principle of turning right and marking the new miracle. This is Sepharadi practice, and the Vilna Gaon and some Ashkenazim differ.
